transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Occupational health suggested I come in. I’ve gotten into a pattern where I skip or push off breakfast and lunch when I’m busy with lab runs or exhibition work, and then when I do eat later, I keep it very small and controlled.
Have you noticed any change in your weight recently?

Yes. My clothes have been getting looser, and the number on the scale has been drifting down. I know that probably sounds concerning, but part of me feels like it means I’m staying focused and keeping control, especially when work feels chaotic.
Do you worry about gaining weight?
Yes. I do. Even if the scale goes up just a little, I feel this sudden panic, like I’m losing control or not being disciplined enough. It sounds extreme when I say it, but that’s how it feels.
Do you ever think about your body shape or appearance when deciding what or how much to eat?

Yes. I do think about it. Like, before I go into the lab, if I catch myself in the mirror, I don’t really see myself as thin. I just notice my stomach or my hips, and then I feel like they make me look careless or not serious enough. That affects what I’ll let myself eat.
Do you feel like eating a normal or large amount of food would make you feel like you're losing control?

Yes. That’s pretty much what happens. I’ve gotten into this pattern where I skip or push off breakfast and lunch when I’m busy in the lab or with exhibition work, and then when I finally do eat, I feel like it has to be something very small and controlled. Eating a normal amount feels like I’m letting things get out of hand.
Do you think others would view you differently if you gained weight?

Yes, I think they would. Or at least I’m afraid they would. If the scale goes up even a tiny bit, I feel this sharp panic, like people will see me as losing discipline or not keeping myself under control.
Does your job or lab work require you to maintain a certain weight or body composition?
No, not officially. My lab work doesn’t require me to be a certain weight or have a certain body composition. It’s more something I put on myself, I guess.
Do you ever make yourself vomit or use laxatives after eating?
I don’t really have anything specific like that to report. I don’t think I’ve been making myself vomit or using laxatives after eating.
Is your fear of gaining weight related to how you think it will affect your job performance or is it more about how you feel about yourself?

It’s more about how I feel about myself. Before I go into the lab, I’ll look in the mirror and I don’t really see someone thin. I just focus on my stomach or my hips, and it makes me feel like I look careless or not serious enough.
Do you think your eating habits are affected by what you believe others might think of your appearance?

Yes, I think so. It’s not always like I’m imagining one specific person judging me, but before I go into the lab I’ll check the mirror and my attention goes right to my stomach or my hips. I don’t see myself as thin. I start feeling like I look careless, or like I won’t be taken seriously, and that affects how I eat.
Do you think you would still restrict your food intake if you didn't worry about what you look like?

I think the appearance worry is a big part of it, but even aside from that, I’ve gotten into this pattern where I push breakfast and lunch aside during lab runs or exhibition work. Then by the time I do eat, I keep it very small and controlled. So… yes, I probably still would, at least in that routine.
Do you feel that your self-worth is closely tied to your weight or body shape?

Yes… I think it is. When I look in the mirror before going into the lab, I don’t really see myself as thin. I mostly notice my stomach or my hips, and then I feel like I look careless or not serious enough. So it does affect how I feel about myself.
Do you think you are currently underweight?

I don’t really think of myself as underweight, no. I know people are concerned, but I feel like they may be overstating it. I’m still functioning, I’m still doing my experiments, and I don’t feel like it’s medically dangerous.
Do you think you would still be afraid of gaining weight if you were at a healthy weight for your height?

Yes. I think I would. Even if someone told me my weight was “healthy,” if the scale went up even a little, I’d feel this immediate panic, like I’m losing control or losing the discipline I’ve worked so hard to keep.
Have your eating habits and concerns about weight affected your relationships with friends or family?

Yes, it has. I’m still getting the important work done and meeting my main deadlines, but I’ve started avoiding things that involve food. I don’t go to lab lunches anymore, and I’ve skipped some informal meals around gallery planning too. So… I guess I’m more isolated from colleagues than I used to be.
Do you think you would see yourself as overweight even if someone else told you that you are at a healthy weight?

Yes… I think I probably would. Even if someone told me I was at a healthy weight, when I look in the mirror before going to the lab, I don’t really see “healthy.” I notice my stomach or my hips, and they look too much to me, like they make me seem careless or not serious enough.
Have you noticed any significant impact of your eating habits on your energy levels or ability to perform daily tasks?

I’m still managing the main things I need to do, like deadlines and work tasks. But it has affected my day-to-day life socially. I’ve stopped going to lab lunches and those informal meals for gallery planning, so I’m definitely more isolated from colleagues than I used to be.
Have you ever eaten an amount of food that you considered excessive in a short period of time?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t think so—not in the way you mean. I can’t think of a time where I ate a large amount in a short period and felt like it was excessive.
Have you ever eaten an amount of food that you considered normal for someone else, but excessive for yourself?

I’m not sure. I guess there are times when something looks normal for someone else, but for me it feels like too much. But I don’t really think of it as “excessive” in the way you’re asking… more like I just feel uncomfortable with it.
Have you ever eaten a large amount of food in a short period of time, feeling like you couldn't stop?
No, I don’t think so. I can’t really think of a time where I ate a large amount quickly and felt like I couldn’t stop.
